title: RPG2: Robust Profile-Guided Runtime Prefetch Generation
problem: Identifying which data to prefetch and when to do so is challenging; prefetches can occur too early (causing eviction of useful data) or too late (missing cache misses), while also competing for limited off-chip memory bandwidth with demand accesses.
motivation: Accurate, well-timed prefetches can dramatically improve processor performance by keeping the pipeline fed and avoiding majority of cache misses.
method: RPG2 learns from watching a program's actual memory accesses, then makes prefetch decisions (deciding what data to load into fast cache ahead of time) customized to that program and processor. Instead of using the same prefetch rules for all programs, it adapts its strategy based on each program's specific memory patterns and the processor's design. The approach carefully balances timing—prefetching early enough to prevent cache misses (when the processor needs data that isn't readily available in fast memory), but not so early that prefetched data gets discarded unused—while managing how much of the memory connection is used for prefetches versus regular memory requests.
key_novelty: Prefetch strategies need to adapt to how a specific program behaves on a specific processor, rather than using prefetch rules that stay the same for everything.
contributions: Handling of timing tradeoffs in prefetch insertion (early eviction vs late arrival)
Bandwidth-aware prefetch generation balancing prefetch and demand access competition
Robustness evaluation showing dependency on program input and microarchitecture

metrics.other: Robustness across program inputs and microarchitectures
